name: nat-vent-outdoor-rises-above-indoor-exit__hvac_fan
description: [hvac_fan twin of golden 'nat-vent-outdoor-rises-above-indoor-exit'; Issue #1193] Nat vent active; outdoor rises above indoor — new directional exit fires before threshold is crossed
source: Issue #1193: hvac_fan twin of golden 'nat-vent-outdoor-rises-above-indoor-exit' (pre-#1140 version, fan configured). The golden is locked and now asserts the no-fan 'paused' result.

verdict.summary: [hvac_fan twin] When outdoor warms above indoor during active nat vent, exits to pause even if still below threshold

events.note: evening: outdoor well below indoor — nat vent eligible. comfort_cool raised to 76 (Issue #392: reactivation gates now also require indoor <= ceiling_threshold for the default/HVAC-fan archetype used here — this scenario tests the directional outdoor-rise exit, not the ceiling gate)
outdoor has risen just above indoor (74.5F > 74.0F); still below threshold 75F — directional exit fires before threshold exit would

assertions.reason: [hvac_fan twin] outdoor 70F < indoor 76F and below threshold 79F; indoor 76F <= ceiling_threshold 76F — nat vent activates
[hvac_fan twin] outdoor 74.5F >= indoor 74.0F — directional exit fires; outdoor still below threshold 79F but airflow no longer beneficial

notes: hvac_fan twin (Issue #1193): with the HVAC fan configured, an open window with usable outdoor air is ventilation (fan on), not a pause. This scenario pins the ventilation/exit/setback decision only; it deliberately does NOT assert the cool setpoint that production also arms during hvac_fan ventilation (nat_vent_ac_assist_armed), which is the rule-3 question tracked in #1142.
